analysis: Only docs/architecture/security/attestation.md was supplied, and without a patch. I saw base lines 264-526 and head lines 1-262, so no head/base pairing and no code. Head, dated 2026-10-12, adds a 'Provider connection control' section (head lines 42-70). It says ProviderLoop+Serve.swift handles app_attest_shadow, trust_status and connection invalidation independently of the ordered inference/model consumer, so a suspended model load does not delay App Attest start or grant writes. It also says connect, disconnect and stream termination clear the old local grant and invalidate the prior App Attest task generation. The claim that cancellation cannot cancel Apple's native call and that a late callback cannot replay an old session's proof through a replacement connection is conditional on the reader having processed invalidation. The coordinator still verifies fresh evidence, expiry and revocation, with no new retry, grace or lifetime (head lines 58-59). This matches the canonical header note, which covers the availability change only. Head lines 63-70 describe an 'endpoint-resumption candidate' answered in CoordinatorClient with the fixed process key and a fresh socket nonce. It claims no Apple work and no local authorization, and says retained evidence must keep original proof deadlines. It is explicitly not deployment or native qualification evidence. TB-011 and T-052..T-058 are the closest threat entries, but a custody-response/resumption path may deserve its own entry once implemented; the next pass should check the code, which is not in this unit. Possible docs inconsistency (not a security finding): head lines 252 and 254 call RuntimeVerified 'gate 5' and RuntimeManifestChecked 'gate 6', while the base routing table (lines 413-422) numbers them 6 and 7. Assertions about the Swift ordering and the daemon grant write were not verifiable here. No security regression is evident from the documentation text alone.
